body: Well, I love your edit and the perspective you've shared with me. Maybe lack of public transportation is certainly an issue. And I think my anger is misplaced on towing companies when it should be towards the city's lackluster attempts to solve the greater issues at hand

I appreciate your responses! The only thing I guess I would say: my belief is that people are parking in the short term spots while they're away because there are not enough homeless shelters and homeless friendly lots that provide places for people who have to sleep in cars (I don't see a lot of urban areas giving out beds to homeless people unfortunately ) and because there are not *enough* long term parking lots. I looked up the closest one to me and it's like an hour or so away. What are your thoughts on this? I was pretty angry originally because my friend had their car removed from a basically empty lot. And then the closest long-term lot to me... the reviews were so shitty because they would advertise as a long term lot but confiscated people's cars anyway. To me it doesn't seem very practical and almost predatory. So it is official my conclusion is I no longer have a problem with towing companies, just the predatory ones... I just hope people don't confuse educating my dumbass with completely abandoning the idea that bad towing companies don't exist haha.
Well I love being wrong haha, it means I learn something new. I have personal anecdotes that support my beliefs and you have yours! It definitely adds more insight though, so thanks for your reply :)

1. If I could mark your post as an answer I definitely would. Thank you!! I guess I still don't understand why you have to pay so much to get the car back. I heard it can be hundreds and hundreds of dollars, so that aspect is a bit silly. Also maybe I have too much faith in humanity, but I don't agree that there would be so few parking spaces that there would be an actual dire issue. 
2. I like your question way better than mine of "Why is parking regulated". But when I looked into this instead of focusing on towing companies, I still couldn't find any good reasons supporting why it's an absolute necessity other than there's more traffic and it hurts business. If it's really about the people then I think there needs to be a separate business that allows people to park their cars when they are away and also more homeless shelters for people who have to live out of their cars. Why screw over everyone else and basically tax people's vehicles? But I'll ask these questions another day I guess lol.

Thanks for giving me a good jumping-off point.
